summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book (Book 12, part 19), Lexy leaves the Enderby house to meet Mr. Houseman, a young man who has agreed to help her, and returns to the city by train. Thinking over the situation, she is confused by Mrs. Enderby's conduct and by Caroline's disappearance before a planned wedding at Wyngate. Back at the house she finds a letter from Houseman, who waited for her in the park and was told by a servant that Miss Enderby had gone to the country with her mother.
one_line: Lexy returns to the city after Caroline's disappearance and finds a letter from Mr. Houseman, who waited in vain for her in the park.
key_facts: Miss Craigie was sent out for a drive so that the chauffeur would be out of the way while Lexy slipped out of the house to the station.
Lexy caught the designated train and returned to the city, taking comfort in the thought of Mr. Houseman's help.
Lexy reasoned that Mr. Houseman said Caroline had promised to meet him last night at a place called Wyngate, where they were to be married.
Caroline had left a letter postmarked Wyngate, but Mr. Houseman said she did not go there.
Lexy reached the Grand Central after dark and chose to walk back to the house, at the risk of being late for dinner.
Lexy described Mrs. Enderby as "confusing" and reflected that she could always think better when walking.
Lexy thought of Mr. Houseman as young like herself, not old and cautious and deliberate, and as her ally.
The servant Annie opened the door with her customary air of disapproval and said Mrs. Enderby had come home in the car half an hour earlier.
Annie said a young man had left a letter about twenty minutes earlier.
Lexy's first thought was that if she had taken a taxi from Grand Central she would have seen him.
The letter was addressed to "Miss Lexy" in a good clear hand, because Houseman did not know her other name.
Houseman wrote that he waited in the park for her all afternoon and went to the house when it got dark.
Houseman wrote that the servant told him Miss Enderby had gone away to the country with her mother that morning.
Houseman wrote: "Please tell Miss Enderby that I understand. I am sorry she didn't tell me".

entities.name: Lexy
entities.role: Protagonist who slips out to the station, returns to the city, and receives Houseman's letter; not given a surname in this part

entities.name: Mr. Houseman
entities.role: Young, sunburned man whom Lexy regards as her ally; Caroline had promised to meet him and marry him

entities.name: Caroline
entities.role: Absent young woman who left the house and was to meet Houseman at Wyngate; called Miss Enderby in the house

entities.name: Mrs. Enderby
entities.role: Mother of Miss Enderby whose plan Lexy carries out; returns home in the car

entities.name: Miss Craigie
entities.role: Companion sent out for a drive so the chauffeur would be removed

entities.name: Annie
entities.role: Servant who opens the door with an air of disapproval and delivers the letter

entities.name: Grand Central
entities.role: Station where Lexy arrives back in the city

entities.name: Wyngate
entities.role: Place where Caroline was to meet Houseman and be married, and the postmark of her letter
